notes: SHIP v1.14.453 - FORGE PARITY P3: THE FOREGROUND WINDOW IS ALL CANONICAL. WHAT CHANGED. P2 made the FOCUSED aisle rack canonical and left its four neighbours as baked photographs, which looked exactly as mixed as it sounds. All five foreground slots are now built by rackGeometry_build - the focused one at full detail, the other four at a new medium tier. THE MEDIUM TIER IS THE SAME BUILDER WITH FEWER PARTS, not a second representation, which is what keeps section 31 no-second-visual-truth true while the five-rack window stays affordable. Medium keeps everything that carries MEANING: the cabinet, the FRONT rails and their EIA-310 perforation, and every device chassis at its true RU in its family colour. It drops what only reads at arm-length: the per-family interiors, the U ticks, the feet, the rear rail pair and the entire rear assembly. full is the DEFAULT, so Build and the focused rack are bit-for-bit what shipped at .452 and only a caller asking for medium gets less. MEASURED, and this is why the tiering was necessary rather than tidy. Naive parity - five canonical racks - was measured at R1 as 5 x 404 = 2020 meshes against an aisle that totalled about 1500, which would have satisfied the visual acceptance and failed no-slowdown in the same breath. The tiered aisle measures 281 meshes total: focused s1:010 at 63 full, s4:099 at 61 medium, s1:001 at 39, s4:100 at 37, empty pad 6, and thirteen background shells at 5 each. PER-SLOT OWNERSHIP. P2 held ONE canonical rack in a module-level handle because only one slot had one. Each slot now owns its own group and its own texture registry and is disposed independently, re-tiered in a single pass on focus change so a slot can never be left holding the previous tier. setLoadout nulls focused before re-focusing, so a window shift re-tiers with the new labels and frees the old geometry; a window with no focusable target re-tiers to nothing rather than stranding the previous window racks. THE BAKED FACE STAYS, AND THAT IS THE CORRECT OUTCOME. The plan said retire DEPLOY_FORGE_FACE_B64 only if proven unreferenced. It is referenced - by the thirteen background shells and by empty pads. Section 33 rules background racks visual context only, remain dark, low-cost geometry, and a single textured plane is the cheapest representation there is. Converting them would contradict both the ruling and the budget, so the photograph keeps the job it is actually right for. A TEST THAT FAILED FOR THE RIGHT REASON, AND THE ASSERTION THAT REPLACED IT. Spec 35 asserted the focused slot had more than three times the meshes of its richest neighbour - true when neighbours were six-mesh photo planes, false by design once they became canonical. Worse, it could never have been right: a SPARSE focused cab at full detail (s1:010, cable-only, 63) legitimately has fewer meshes than a DENSE neighbour at medium (s4:099, nineteen devices, 61), so comparing different racks measures how populated they are, not what tier they are drawn at. The tiers are now compared on the SAME rack built both ways, plus a foreground-versus-background split asserting every labelled foreground slot is canonical while the shells are not. RUNS (phone-webkit, each spec ALONE): 35 = 3, 32 = 3, 31 = 4, 33 = 4, 34 = 3, 30 = 4, 02-build-forge = 14 including the x10 aisle round trip, 08-forge-layout = 17 passed with 1 skipped. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, 12 style blocks brace-balanced, 0 bare LF, three-stamp lockstep at .453. DEVICE-VERIFY: load a Master and open the aisle. PASS is every rack in the front row reading as a real cabinet with frame, rails and device trays in family colours - no CoreWeave photo faces among them - the background racks still dark and cheap, and walking across ten racks with no slowdown. FAIL is a photo face in the front row, a blank foreground rack, or the aisle stuttering as you walk.
